newsitem.title: FINLAND: Parliament speaker stuns Finns with sex talk.
newsitem.headline: Parliament speaker stuns Finns with sex talk.

text.p: Nearly a century after women in Finland broke new ground by being the first in Europe to vote, the female speaker of parliament has shattered a new barrier with a highly explicit book about her sex life.

Finns are queuing by the hundred to buy "Fluttering Flame", by 54-year old Conservative Riitta Uosukainen, a former education minister who as speaker ranks second only to President Martti Ahtisaari in the Finnish political hierarchy.
Fellow politicians have slammed the book -- which is very abusive about some of them -- saying it irreparably undermines the prestige of her position and the Finnish political system.
But ordinary people are enthusiastic about her frankness.

Published last week, its first run of 17,000 sold out in three days and its publishers said on Monday they have had to order extra paper to cope with the demand. On Sunday churchgoers flocked by the thousand to see Uosukainen at an evening service.

Ostensibly an epistolary novel of imaginary letters written to and about political colleagues and friends, the book contains one stunningly frank "letter" to Uosukainen's husband, a high-ranking soldier, about a weekend in 1996.

"Thanks for the wonderful weekend, for all the good loving and love-making. We had a fabulous time together," writes Uosukainen, believed by many to be preparing to run for president after Ahtisaari's term ends in the year 2000.
"The waterbed is tremendous; it doesn't creak -- and, oh, that slosh of fucking," she continues.

Uosukainen, a majestic, strong-jawed former teacher who only sees her husband at weekends, enjoys wide popularity. As parliamentary speaker, she has demonstrated strong skills in bringing members of the house to order.
Such explicitness may fit into the cliche of sexual frankness and women's liberation associated with countries like Sweden. But in relatively conservative Finland, it is explosive.
One columnist in the daily Ilta-Sanomat said that any male speaker who had penned such a book would have been labelled a chauvinist.
Uosukainen said she wrote the erotic chapter -- which deals only with marital sex -- because sex is important to her.

"It would have been deceptive if I had skipped the erotica. People often ask me how I can keep going. I wanted to show that eroticism is a source of energy for me so others too would see it's part of a normal life," she told the daily Iltalehti.
"There shouldn't be anything strange about the fact that a middle-aged woman enjoys herself," she added.

Uosukainen has defended the work by arguing that the region of Finland she comes from, Carelia, is known to produce the most sensual Finns. In the letter, she writes of Carelian women who ask their homecoming husbands:
"'Do you want to eat, drink, take a sauna or fuck?' We are in that situation weekly, and have altered the programme as we see best. But best of all is when we've begun fucking first."

Commentators are still undecided on what the consequences could be for her political career and her chances as president. But they agree the book has injected an entirely new element into Finland's secretive, sometimes sleepy, political culture.
Uosukainen's husband has made little public comment, beyond confirming her remarks: "The waterbed is good," he told Iltalehti. "Absolutely. It's good for my back."
